# Nutri-Trust

Nutri-Trust is a free web app for Indian households that combines packaged-food
label interpretation with pantry expiry tracking. A user scans a barcode to get
a 1-5 nutrition reading with the concerns and positives behind it, adds items to
a pantry by barcode, receipt photo or manual entry, and receives Indian recipes
that prioritise whatever is closest to spoiling. It was built as an
undergraduate minor project at Manipal Institute of Technology and is not a
commercial product.

Most of the application sits behind a sign-in, because a pantry is personal
data. The pages listed below are the ones reachable without an account.

## Pages

- [Home / sign in](https://nutri-trusto.vercel.app/): entry point; redirects to
  the dashboard once signed in.
- [Privacy policy](https://nutri-trusto.vercel.app/privacy): what personal
  information is collected, why, which third parties process it, and how to
  request deletion.

## What the app does

- Barcode scanning, resolved against Open Food Facts (India index first, then
  the global index), producing a NutriTrust score from 1 to 5.
- Nutrition-label and expiry-date scanning by photo, used when a product is not
  in the database.
- Receipt scanning to add several pantry items at once, reading the real
  purchase date printed on the receipt.
- Expiry tracking with risk levels, and notifications as items approach expiry.
- Allergen detection from ingredient text across seven allergen classes. When no
  ingredient data exists the app reports "unknown" rather than "safe".
- Recipe generation restricted to Indian home cooking, prioritising items
  expiring first and respecting a vegetarian, eggtarian or non-vegetarian
  preference.
- Household sharing, shopping list, scan history and an impact dashboard.

## Limits worth stating

- The nutrition score is derived from Open Food Facts data. It has not been
  validated by a nutritionist and is not medical or dietary advice.
- Allergen detection is keyword matching over ingredient text, not a laboratory
  result. It cannot detect cross-contamination.
- The app performs no live FSSAI compliance check. No public machine-readable
  FSSAI API exists.
- Recipes are generated by a language model and are written for the ingredients
  a user happens to have, so they do not correspond to any published recipe.
